newsitem.title: USA: Anchor Gaming jumps on takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Anchor Gaming jumps on takeover talk.

text.p: Shares of Las Vegas-based Anchor Gaming racked up a 13 percent gain by midday Thursday on speculation Chief Executive Officer Stan Fulton is looking at an outright sale of the company.
Financial analysts said the company could fetch anywhere from $55 to $60 a share as a whole, or it could be split into parts. Anchor stock was up 5-1/2 to 46-1/2.
Late Wednesday, Anchor Gaming issued a press release saying it had hired Morgan Stanley & Co to advise it on a possible sale or merger.
Anchor Gaming officials were not immediately available to comment on Thursday.

Financial analysts said Fulton controls roughly 7.0 million of the company's 13.7 million shares outstanding, and they said the chief executive, who is known for his silence with the investment community, was likely upset at a recent tumble in the stock price and decided to sell.
"His forte has always been starting up companies and I'm not sure in my own mind that he wants to be a CEO of a developed company," said Steve Schneider, analyst at St. Louis-based Stifel Nicolaus.
On November 12, Anchor Gaming shares dropped nearly eight points after it announced it would not expand its highly profitable casino in Black Hawk, Colo. The stock has since regained the lost ground.

With a possible price ranging from $750 to $825 million, analysts said a major hotel and casino group like Hilton Hotels Corp, ITT Corp or Mirage Inc might be an acquiror because of the Black Hawk casino.
Analysts also look to equipment maker International Gaming Technology Inc as a possible acquiror because of Anchor's slot routes and new game called "Wheel of Gold."
In recent research, BT Securities analyst Robin Farley said slot routes give solid, single-digit growth prospects and noted the game business is Anchor's fastest growing segment.
Because Anchor has three businesses -- casinos, slot routes, and gaming machine -- it could be sold off in parts.

Farley valued the routes between $4.20 and $4.80 a share and the machine buiness at $27 to $30 a share. She values current operations at Black Hawk from $13.80 to $17.25 a share and a smaller casino in Colorado from $1.08 to $1.35 a share.
Adding to the valuation is over $80 million in cash Anchor had planned to use for expansion, analysts said.
